rationale: Both independently surface the same core issues (WER double-resample, VAE config mutation, dropped language/dialect mapping, unexplained +2 stop-step) with strong file/line actionability. X's headline VAE finding claims to have 'verified locally against the installed transformers' that mutating config.num_hidden_layers truncates the running encoder to 4 layers — but this contradicts the ground-truth maintainer clarification (LHXuuu) that the encoder module is already constructed before the mutation and its real depth is unaffected, only config metadata is stale; X presents fabricated-looking verification output as high-severity fact, which is a serious grounding failure. Y frames the same hunk correctly as a metadata-only bug (config now misreports num_hidden_layers) matching the actual reviewer concern, and consistently ties every finding to quoted diff/file evidence with a validated-claims ledger, giving it higher precision and slightly better recall of the real reviewer thread.
